### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, touching **41** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**25** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e1dac19257184aa28115ead12c4ce0918d55b2b4`.

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **14** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **224** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **161** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **161**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **57** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e1dac19257184aa28115ead12c4ce0918d55b2b4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `39d564057e55f81f5f6799713909eb06b0645f63` — the merge of head `44f83463eae437ec760d31c6f9a7863f8b2949b3` into base `e1dac19257184aa28115ead12c4ce0918d55b2b4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 39d564057e55f81f5f6799713909eb06b0645f63 && git checkout 39d564057e55f81f5f6799713909eb06b0645f63
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e1dac19257184aa28115ead12c4ce0918d55b2b4 44f83463eae437ec760d31c6f9a7863f8b2949b3 && git checkout -B drift-repro e1dac19257184aa28115ead12c4ce0918d55b2b4 && git merge --no-ff 44f83463eae437ec760d31c6f9a7863f8b2949b3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e1dac19257184aa28115ead12c4ce0918d55b2b4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e1dac19257184aa28115ead12c4ce0918d55b2b4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `3b340ba21456c28faab599a6e2c9eeb23a382048`
Local-runs: none

Reviewed 2026-11-06T20:37Z on the net diff `origin/main...3b340ba214` (merge base `41dc302496`, 11 files, +799 −4), the PR body, the file list and the head's check-runs. The rule's semantics were judged against the cited code on `main` only.

Check-runs on this head, as they stand: 61 runs: 17 success, 8 skipped, 0 failure, 36 still in progress. The success runs include Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Type Check · source gates, Check Documentation Links and Dogfood Regression Gate. Still in progress: Build Core, Build Docs, Build and E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Test Core 1–8 of 8, Test UI 1–16 of 16, Type Check UI, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, and Lint · CI, release and engine gates, docs and code guards, repo and tooling gates, scoped slot lookup and corpus. `check:docs-transcript-drift`, which judges the 63→64 edits, runs in one of the Lint jobs that has not finished. None of these is red yet. None of them is green yet either.

### ① Derived judgments

**Public surface (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`): right.** It adds `validateRollupSourceVisibility`, `SECURITY_ROLLUP_SOURCE_UNREADABLE`, `SECURITY_ROLLUP_SOURCE_ROW_SCOPED`, `RollupSourceVisibilityFinding` and `RollupSourceVisibilitySeverity`. They follow the existing shape for security rules (the `SecurityFinding` / `SecuritySeverity` pair beside them). Nothing is removed or renamed.

**Rule ids: right.** `security-rollup-source-unreadable` (warning) and `security-rollup-source-row-scoped` (info) sit in the `security-` family. Arms (i) and (ii) share one id, and that holds up: both tell the author the same consequence and give the same remedy. Each id has an `os explain` entry in `RULE_EXPLANATIONS`.

**Registry entry: right on every field except the reason text.**
- `tier: 'advisory'`: right. The rule emits only `warning` and `info`, so no stack that loaded before is refused.
- `input: 'parsed'`: right. Every key it reads is declared by the spec (`enabled`, `operation`, `readable` and their defaults).
- `commands: ALL`: right.
- `surfaces: CLI_ONLY`: acceptable for this PR (see ③(1)).
- `surfaceReason`: present, but it names the wrong precedent (S4).
- Count: the registry on `origin/main` has 63 entries and the head has 64. The CLI prints `registered.length` (compile.ts:558, validate.ts:514), so the four transcript edits from 63 to 64 match the tree. No other `(63)` is left in `content/`.

**Docs.** The four-doors row is correct: the columns are validate / build / lint / runtime publish, and the row reads ✓ ✓ ✓ —, which is CLI-only. The `#the-one-gate-four-doors` anchor exists. The new sentence in `fields.mdx` ("`os lint`, `os validate` and `os build` warn about each such set") and its remedy clause promise more than the rule does (M1, S2).

**Where "can read" matches the runtime.** These points were checked against `main`:
- The set's explicit object entry, otherwise its `'*'` entry, and a private object covered by `'*'` only through View All / Modify All. Same as `resolveObjectPermission` in `permission-evaluator.ts`.
- `isPrivate` means `access.default === 'private'`. Same as `security-plugin.ts`.
- The read verb goes through `objectPermissionGrants`, the same fold the evaluator uses.
- A field with no entry is readable. `readable` defaults to `true` in `FieldPermissionSchema`. `readable: false` beside a `when` is refused at parse, so no hide is ever conditional.
- A `readable: false` next to View All on the parent does nothing, as `superuserFieldVote` decides. An explicit entry shadows a super-user `'*'` entry, as `holdsSuperuserBypass` in core decides; the lint copy is identical.
- Which RLS policies apply: `enabled`, the object or `'*'`, and `select` / `all`, as in `RLSCompiler.getApplicablePolicies`. The `positions` domain is named in the message rather than judged.
- `defaultRowScope` gives way to any applicable policy the set holds, as `object-default-row-scope.ts` does.

**Where "can read" does not match the runtime.**

- **M1 (must-fix): the ADR-0066 D3 capability gate is not modelled on either side.**
  The runtime refuses an object read when the caller lacks a capability in the object's `requiredPermissions` read bucket, however permissive the grants are. View All does not lift this (`objectReadAdmission`, step 4). It also hides a field whose `requiredPermissions` the caller does not fully hold. That fold runs after the super-user vote, so View All does not lift it either (`foldFieldRequiredPermissions`). The rule reads neither the field's or object's `requiredPermissions` nor the set's `systemPermissions`. What the author is then told:
  - (a) Nothing, when the aggregated child field or the child object is gated by a capability the set lacks. This is the platform's own way of keeping a sensitive field from a population, which makes it the textbook case for this rule.
  - (b) A warning, plus a remedy that changes nothing, when the summary column or the parent object is gated by a capability the set lacks. In that case the set cannot read the roll-up at all.
  - (c) The View All parent hint says the column "cannot be hidden from this set while it holds View All or Modify All". That is false for a column that carries `requiredPermissions`.
  - (d) The child-side skip claims a View All / Modify All holder "reads every child row and field". That is false for a capability-gated field.

  Sentence (d) is in the explain entry, the changeset body (which ships as `CHANGELOG.md`), the PR body and the docblock. The fix: judge `requiredPermissions` against the set's own `systemPermissions`, field-level and object-level read bucket, on both parent and child. Add one negative and one positive test for each side. Then align the sentences in the explain entry, the changeset and `fields.mdx`.

- **S1 (should-fix): the View All / Modify All skip on the child is wider than the runtime for arm (iii).**
  The read filter skips business RLS for a super-user only when the object's posture permits it: private access, tenancy disabled, or auth-managed (`security-plugin-rls-filter.ts`, where `superuserBypass` is `false` unless `posturePermits`). On a public child, a View All holder's own read policies and the child's `defaultRowScope` still narrow the rows it reads. The case "the set holds View All or Modify All on the child" pins silence for a public child that carries a `select` policy. Apply the arm-(iii) half of the skip only to a private child. The field half can stay.

- **S2 (should-fix): the remedy does not say that it reaches every holder of the set.**
  In the field merge (`getFieldPermissions`), only sets that declare an entry vote. So `fields["…summary"]: { readable: false }` on one set hides the column from every holder of that set, including holders who read the child through another set. A co-held set with no entry for the column casts no vote and does not restore the read. Six of the showcase's nine warnings are on `showcase_member_default`, the additive `everyone` baseline (`isDefault: true`). Following the hint there would hide the expense totals from contributors who read the lines. The hint and the explain entry should say this, and name the alternative: declare `readable: true` on the column in the sets that should keep it.

- **S3 (should-fix): `summaryOperations.filter` reads child fields that are not judged.**
  A filtered count or sum over a predicate on a field the set cannot read tells the reader something about that field. Examples: a count where a hidden band field matches, or the showcase's filtered `rejected_count` / `approved_amount` shapes. Either judge the filter's field references under arm (i), or state in the explain entry that they are not judged.

- **Per-set judgment** (a holder of two sets reads their union) is declared plainly and is a fair limit for a rule that never refuses.

**Dev deviation: messages pinned by inline snapshots.** Accepted. This is the first `toMatchInlineSnapshot` under `packages/`. It pins the exact one-line text the author reads, and that text is the contract here. The only cost is that `vitest -u` can rewrite a snapshot without anyone deciding to. A reviewer should therefore read any snapshot change in a diff as a change to the message.

### ② Semver level

**The `patch` changeset on `@objectstack/lint` matches what the diff publishes.**
- No other package changes. `content/` is not a package.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing an author can write is added, refused or redefined.
- AGENTS.md post-task step 3 maps `none` to `patch`.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right: the package's public exports widen, and nothing that passed is refused.
- A new warning failing an `os lint --strict` run is the documented opt-in of `--strict`, not a narrowing. The changeset says so, as the `30804-lint-namespace-prefix-every-name` precedent does.
- Both declaration lines open a line in the PR body and in the changeset. Check Changeset is green.

The M1 fix reads keys the spec already declares, so the level stays `none` / `patch`.

### ③ Boundary flags

**(1) Runtime publish gate. Answer: A for this PR. B as a separate card, sent to the maintainer.**
- For B: hosted Studio, REST `/meta` and MCP authors configure permission sets at the runtime door and have no other door.
- For B: the per-write snapshot has carried `permissions` and `objects` since #8309.
- For B: a non-refusing permission-set rule has already crossed on `permission` writes alone (`validateRetiredPermissionResidue`, #17936).
- For B: the runtime object universe would also resolve the child objects of other packages, which the CLI view leaves unjudged.
- Against C: object writes fall under the object-door volume fence. That is a separate UX decision, and this rule should not be the one to open it.

S4 (should-fix): the shipped `surfaceReason` treats a `permission`-write crossing as needing the object-door volume fence's ruling. That fence is written about object rules. Reword it to give the actual reason: there is no per-write measurement on permission writes yet, and object writes would be fenced.

**(2) Record sharing in the row-scope arm. Answer: no, not in this PR.**
- On an owner-scoped private child, every set without View All defaults to `own` depth (`getEffectiveScope`). A note there would fire on nearly every lookup roll-up over a private child.
- A `controlled_by_parent` detail takes its access from the master, so for the master-detail roll-up shape sharing narrows nothing the reader cannot already see through the parent.
- The explain entry already says `sharingModel` / `readScope` are not read, which is the honest statement.
- If this is wanted later, a separate card can scope it narrowly: a private child that is not `controlled_by_parent`, where the set declares a `readScope` narrower than `org`. Measure it on the example apps first.

**(3) Intentional roll-ups warn permanently. Answer: leave it in this PR. Send the decision to a separate card. Do not edit the showcase sets as a reflex.**
- Per S2, the hint's remedy applied to the `everyone` baseline would also hide totals from contributors.
- An acknowledgement key is a new key an author can write: `Metadata-protocol: added`, `minor`, with its own ruling. It should be designed once across warning-only rules, not for one rule.
- The card should choose between:
  - (a) Treating an explicitly authored `readable: true` on the summary column, in that set, as the acknowledgement. No new key is needed, but the parse materializes `readable: true` as a default, so the rule would have to read the normalized input to tell an authored value from a default.
  - (b) A generic acknowledgement key.
- Then fix the showcase per the decision. Nine standing warnings in the reference app teach authors to ignore the channel, so this should not wait long.

Implemented-by: `claude/sec-hardening-r14`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qibvynRbCtMndW8EHNGc`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `44f83463eae437ec760d31c6f9a7863f8b2949b3`
Local-runs: none

Reviewed 2026-11-06T22:32Z on the net diff `origin/main...44f83463ea` (merge base `41dc302496`, 11 files, +1224 −4), the delta `3b340ba214..44f83463ea` (7 files, +556 −131), the PR body as rewritten at this head, the file list and the head's check-runs. The rule's semantics were judged against the cited code on `main`. Every cited runtime and spec file is byte-unchanged between the merge base and `origin/main` at `bd1b7685fc`, and `main` still registers 63 author-time rules, so the 63→64 transcript edits still match.

This record supersedes the FAIL on `3b340ba214` (2026-11-06T20:37:41Z).

Check-runs on this head: 69 runs, 59 success, 10 skipped, 0 failure, none in progress. Nine of the ten required contexts are success: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Type Check UI, Test UI, Build & E2E UI and Live E2E UI. `Lint UI` is skipped. Check Changeset, PR-body guards, every Lint · job (which carries `check:docs-transcript-drift` and `check:doc-authoring`), the Type Check · jobs and Dogfood Regression Gate are success.

### ① Derived judgments

**The previous must-fix and should-fixes, judged in the tree.**

- **M1 (capability gate): answered.**
  - Object side. `objectReadCapabilities` reads the `string[]` form as gating every operation, and the per-operation map through its `read` bucket alone. That is `normalizeRequiredPermissions` followed by `requiredCapsForOperation(spec, 'find')` on `main`: `find` maps to `allowRead`, which maps to the `read` bucket, and the map form's `all` bucket is always empty. `PerOperationRequiredPermissionsSchema` is `.strict()` over `read` / `create` / `update` / `delete`, so no other key can carry a read gate.
  - Field side. `fieldCapabilities` reads the field's `requiredPermissions`, which is what `getObjectSecurityMeta` collects into `fieldRequiredPermissions`, from both the list and the map form of `fields`.
  - The fold. `missingCapabilities` is the AND-gate against the set's own `systemPermissions`, which is `getSystemPermissions` restricted to one set. It ignores the super-user bits. That matches `objectReadAdmission` step 4, which runs ahead of the grant, and `foldFieldRequiredPermissions`, which runs after the `getFieldPermissions` super-user vote in `maskOperationResult`.
  - Both sides of the roll-up are covered. The parent object and the summary column go through all three gates before a pair is judged. The child object, the aggregated child field and the filter fields go through the same gates.
  - The four sentences the previous record named are corrected:
    - (a) A gated child object or field now warns, with the missing capabilities named.
    - (b) A gated parent or summary column is now silent, including under View All on the parent.
    - (c) The View All parent hint now says that `readable: false` does not hide a field from a set holding either bit. It no longer says the column cannot be hidden.
    - (d) "reads every child row and field" is gone from the docblock, the explain entry, the changeset and the PR body. A tree-wide grep finds no copy left.
  - Tests cover both forms, the controls (a held capability, and a map that gates only writes) and View All not lifting either gate.
- **S1 (View All skip on the child): answered.** `postureSkipsRowSecurityForSuperuser` takes four postures: `access.default: 'private'`, `tenancy.enabled === false`, `systemFields.tenant === false` and `managedBy: 'better-auth'`. Those are the runtime's `posturePermits` (`meta.isPrivate || meta.tenancyDisabled || meta.isBetterAuthManaged`), with `tenancyDisabled` spelled as the same two clauses in `getObjectSecurityMeta`. The `tenancyDisabledCache` does not enter `posturePermits`, and it does not enter the rule either. The skip now applies only to arm (iii). The field half still comes from `fieldHidden`'s super-user vote, and the capability half is never skipped. On a public child, the runtime's `superuserBypass` is `false`, `collectRLSPolicies` runs and an empty collection falls through to the child's `defaultRowScope`, which is what the two public-child cases pin. The control case (a tenancy-off child without the bypass, still noted) is there.
- **S2 (reach of the fix line): answered in the hint and the explain entries, and partly in `fields.mdx` (S6).** The hint now says that the entry hides the column from every holder of the set, that a co-held set with no entry does not restore it, that View All or Modify All on the parent in a co-held set does, and that `readable: true` keeps it for chosen holders. That is the `getFieldPermissions` merge, where only declaring sets vote and `superuserFieldVote` applies afterwards.
- **S3 (filter fields): answered for bare keys.** `filterFieldKeys` walks `summaryOperations.filter` with the shared `walkFilterFieldKeys`. That covers `$and` / `$or`, `$not`, operator leaves and implicit equality. It also covers the AST and view-rule shapes, which the parse refuses before this rule runs on `filter`, so they are harmless extras. Each bare key goes through the field gates. A `count`'s `field` is still not judged, and its `filter` is.
- **S4 (surfaceReason precedent): answered.** The reason now says that no per-write measurement exists of what a `permission` save hands the rule. That is exactly the measurement the `validateRetiredPermissionResidue` entry on `main` records as taken before it crossed on `permission` writes. Object writes are named as falling under `RUNTIME_OBJECT_ADVISORY_VOLUME`. The tracker id now sits in the adjacent comment, not the runtime string.

**Tested against the new logic, beyond the fixes: held.**
- Map form against list form, and a map that gates only `update` / `delete`: no read gate, which matches `requiredCapsForOperation`.
- View All on the child against a gated child field or object: it still warns, because the field fold runs after the super-user vote and the object gate runs ahead of the grant.
- View All on the parent against a gated summary column: silent, because the column is hidden whatever the bits.
- A `'*'` View All entry on a private child: it grants the read, as `resolveObjectPermission` does, and it counts for the posture skip, as `holdsSuperuserBypass` in core does (the lint copy is identical).
- `rowLevelSecurity[].operation` is required by the spec, so the `select` / `all` test does not depend on a default.
- Arm order (object, value, filter, row) and one finding per pair: the first unreadable filter key names the finding. That is a fair choice for a one-line verdict.

**New should-fixes.**

- **S5 (should-fix): a dotted or nested filter key is skipped whole, including its first hop, which is a child field.**
  - Both spellings of a relation condition are skipped. `{ 'account.region': 'emea' }` reaches the walker dotted. `{ account: { region: 'emea' } }` is turned into the dotted `account.region` by `conditionFieldKeys`.
  - `filterFieldKeys` drops every key that contains a dot. So a set with `fields["invoice_line.account"]: { readable: false }` reads a count filtered through `account` and is told nothing. The docblock's own arm 3, "it cannot read a child field `summaryOperations.filter` tests", covers that hop.
  - Proposed fix: judge the first segment (`field.split('.')[0]`) as a child field under the same three gates. Leave the far object unjudged, or judge it against the stack's object graph.
  - Otherwise, narrow the wording to what the tree does in all three places: the explain entry, the docblock and the PR body. Each would say: "a relation key, dotted or nested, is not judged, its first hop included". The explain entry also calls the judged keys "top-level", although keys inside `$and` / `$or` / `$not` are judged too. "Bare" is the accurate word.
- **S6 (should-fix): the remedy sentence in `fields.mdx` leaves out the View All caveat that the hint and the explain entry carry.** It reads "set `readable: false` on the summary field in that set: it hides the field from every holder of the set". On a set holding View All or Modify All on the parent, that entry is inert (`superuserFieldVote`), so a reader who follows the doc changes nothing. The fix is one clause: "(a set holding View All or Modify All on the parent must drop that bit first)".

**Non-blocking notes.**
- The registry entry's leading comment in `authoring-rules.ts` still lists only "a hidden source field, an unreadable child object, or child rows a row-level policy narrows". It does not mention the capability gate or the filter fields.
- The rule reads posture from the authored stack. A deployment that declares an object platform-global gets `systemFields.tenant: false` from the registry at boot. The rule cannot see that, so for a View All holder there it may emit an `info` note that the runtime would not apply. This is the off-stack limit every CLI-only rule has.
- On a child field that carries both a `maskingRule` and `requiredPermissions`, a caller without the capability is served the masked value. The finding's "cannot read without capability" is then loosely true: the set reads the field masked, never in full. It is not misleading enough to change.
- PR body: "CI on 44f83463ea: 57 success, 8 skipped" is a snapshot. The head now reads 59 success and 10 skipped. The "43 cases" claim matches the tree.
- Inline snapshots: the previous record's acceptance carries forward. Five `toMatchInlineSnapshot` sites pin the message and hint text. Read any snapshot change in a diff as a change to the message.

### ② Semver level

**The `patch` changeset on `@objectstack/lint` matches what the diff publishes now.**
- The delta does not touch `packages/lint/src/index.ts`. The five exports and two types are the ones the previous record judged, and no other package moves.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. The capability fold reads `requiredPermissions` and `systemPermissions`, which the spec already declares. Nothing an author can write is added, refused or redefined. AGENTS.md post-task step 3 maps `none` to `patch`.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right. The package's public exports widen, and nothing that passed before is refused. A new warning failing a `--strict` run is the documented opt-in, not a narrowing.
- Both declaration lines are line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset, and Check Changeset is green.
- The S5 and S6 fixes read declared keys and edit prose, so the level stays `none` / `patch`.

### ③ Boundary flags

The delta changes none of the three answers. They carry forward from the previous record.

- **(1) Runtime publish gate: A for this PR (CLI-only). B as a separate card, sent to the maintainer.** The S4 rewording now states this answer's actual reason in `surfaceReason`. Crossing on `permission` writes needs the per-write measurement the residue rule took first. Crossing on `object` writes stays behind the object-door volume fence. Neither is opened here.
- **(2) Record sharing in the row-scope arm: no, not in this PR.** The explain entry and the PR body say that `sharingModel` / `readScope` are not read, and that is the honest statement. A later card could scope it narrowly, as the previous record described.
- **(3) Intentional roll-ups that warn permanently: the acknowledgement question is its own card.** Do not edit the showcase sets as a reflex.
